newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains cattle sales active at $71 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains cattle sales active at $71 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle near midday Thursday sold in fairly active trade at $71.00 per cwt, down $2.00 from last week's top, feedlot sources said.
Prices were pressured by weak beef prices, they said.

About 12,000 head had sold in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area as of midday Thursday, which brought the week-to-date figure close to 67,000, sources there said. About 39,100 head were sold Wednesday, according to USDA.
In Kansas, 16,700 head were sold by midday Thursday, bringing the week to date to 37,000 including 8,800 head or about 24 percent previously contracted or formulated cattle, USDA said.

This week's standoff between packers and cattle feeders was broken late Wednesday when one feedlot in the Texas Panhandle sold at packer bids of $71.00 per cwt after asking $73.00 since Monday, market sources said. Once a number of cattle sold at $71.00, other feedlots followed suit, they said.
